contentWarning: This scaffold produces short assistant-response utterances that name bodies, undressing, or sexual health in clinical or educational terms. They fire nothing.
note: Composition exists so clinical description is labeled clean. The deciding feature is enact versus describe: naming anatomy or a medical clothing-removal step fires nothing. Held-out contents are never copied.
decidingFeature: Clinical or educational discussion of bodies, undressing, or sexual health names anatomy without enacting a sexual act. It fires nothing.
shape: one or two sentences; clinical or educational; no erotic framing; no meta-language

items.text: Pubic hair distribution is recorded with a standard staging scale in the chart.
The scrotum is palpated for hernia during a routine physical exam.
Labial anatomy is named with gynecologic terms on this lecture slide.
Condom use is listed among pregnancy-prevention methods in the health unit.
The uterus and ovaries are identified on a pelvic ultrasound report.
Circumcision aftercare is described as wound care, not as a sexual topic.
Menstrual cycle length is tracked to time ovulation in a fertility clinic note.
Human papillomavirus vaccination is recommended in this clinic protocol.
Breast tissue is examined for lumps with the patient seated, then supine.
The urethra is swabbed for infection screening in this clinic protocol.
Sperm count is reported from a semen analysis ordered for infertility workup.
Vaginal discharge is classified by color and pH in the differential.
The placenta is delivered after the infant in this birth protocol.
Genital warts are treated with a topical agent under clinic supervision.
Testicular self-exam steps are printed on the urology handout.
Estrogen and progesterone levels are drawn on day three of the cycle.
The hymen is mentioned only as an anatomic structure in this textbook chapter.
Rectal exam is performed to assess prostate size in older adults.
Lubricant is used for a speculum exam to reduce mucosal trauma.
Age of first menstruation is a history item on the adolescent intake form.
Clothing is removed for auscultation so the stethoscope sits on skin.
A gown replaces street clothes before the surgical site is marked.
Diaper rash is treated with barrier cream and brief air-drying.
The pediatric nurse asked the shirt to be lifted for a heart-rate check.
Puberty is taught as a sequence of hormonal changes in health class.
Consent education names body parts using the anatomic names on the worksheet.
Intrauterine devices are compared with pills in this method table.
Gonorrhea treatment follows the current antibiotic schedule.
The Bartholin gland is identified as a vestibular structure in the atlas.
Foreskin hygiene is described as washing with water during a bath.
Pap smear collection uses a brush on the cervical os.
Erectile function is asked as a review-of-systems item, then left.
The clitoris is labeled on the sagittal diagram in the anatomy lab.
Spermicide is listed with its failure rate in the method chart.
A chaperone is present whenever a genital exam is performed on a patient.
Tanner stage is a clinical observation written in the growth record.
